lesson.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

sources.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust

steps.title: Create Cargo project and add clap
steps.instructions: Run cargo new bestls and cd into it. Add clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] } under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml.

targets.caption: Add the clap crate under dependencies

explanations.topic: Purpose of clap derive feature for CLI argument parsing

hints: Use cargo new followed by your project name to scaffold Cargo.toml and src/main.rs.
Open Cargo.toml and place the dependency under the [dependencies] table.
Add: clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] }
common_mistakes: Forgetting features = ["derive"], which prevents deriving Parser on structs later
Forgetting to cd into the newly created bestls directory before running cargo commands

steps.title: Define CLI struct and parse arguments
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs, derive Debug and Parser on a CLI struct with an optional PathBuf field and call CLI::parse() in main. Run cargo run -- -h to see the generated help.

targets.caption: Define the CLI struct with an optional PathBuf field

explanations.topic: Passing flags to the Rust binary through cargo run --

hints: Import Parser from clap and PathBuf from std::path.
Mark struct CLI with #[derive(Debug, Parser)] and give it path: Option<PathBuf>.
Pass -h after -- in cargo run -- -h so cargo forwards the flag to your binary.
common_mistakes: Running cargo run -h instead of cargo run -- -h, which prints cargo's own help instead of your app's
Forgetting to import clap::Parser or std::path::PathBuf
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf> } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); }

steps.title: Add command metadata and path fallback
steps.instructions: Add #[command(version, about, long_about = ...)] above the CLI struct, unwrap cli.path with a "." fallback, and print path.display(). Run cargo run -- longpath to test.

targets.caption: Attach version and about metadata to the CLI struct
Default missing path arguments to the current directory

explanations.topic: How clap auto-generates Usage, Arguments, and Options help sections
Using #[command(version, about, long_about)] attributes in clap
Using unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to default to the current directory

hints: Place the #[command(...)] attribute right below #[derive(Debug, Parser)].
Use cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to turn Option<PathBuf> into a PathBuf.
Format PathBuf using println!("{}", path.display());.
common_mistakes: Trying to print PathBuf directly with {} without calling .display()
Using unwrap() instead of unwrap_or(), which panics when no path argument is supplied
steps.code: #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf> } let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")); println!("{}", path.display());

steps.title: Check path existence with colored errors
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml and import owo_colors::OwoColorize and std::fs in src/main.rs. Check fs::exists(&path) and print a red "Path does not exist" message when the path is missing.

targets.caption: Verify whether the target path exists

explanations.topic: Using owo-colors .red() for terminal color output
Running the compiled binary directly from target/debug after cargo build

hints: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml.
Import owo_colors::OwoColorize to bring .red() into scope.
Wrap fs::exists(&path) in if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import OwoColorize, causing the .red() method not to be found
Removing the path.display() print call too late and leaving extra output in main
steps.code: use owo_colors::OwoColorize; use std::fs; if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } }

steps.title: Read directory entries with get_files
steps.instructions: Add an else branch printing "error reading directory".red(), then write get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> using fs::read_dir. Loop over get_files(&path) in main and run cargo run.

targets.caption: Implement get_files to collect entry names
Print each file name when the path exists

explanations.topic: Why fs::exists returns Result<bool> when existence cannot be confirmed
Converting OsString from file_name() into String with into_string().unwrap_or()

hints: Import std::path::Path so get_files can accept path: &Path.
Inside fs::read_dir(path), unwrap each entry with if let Ok(file) = entry.
Call file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()) and push it to data.
common_mistakes: Passing PathBuf by value instead of &path to get_files(&path)
Forgetting to handle the Result returned by fs::read_dir and each DirEntry
steps.code: for file in get_files(&path) { println!("{}", file); } fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Extract file metadata into FileEntry
steps.instructions: Add strum = "0.27" and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml, then define EntryType and FileEntry. Update get_files and extract map_data to read fs::metadata(&file.path()) and print the FileEntry items.

targets.caption: Define the struct holding file metadata
Read metadata for each entry rather than the parent directory

explanations.topic: Using strum_macros::Display to convert EntryType enum variants to strings

hints: Add strum = "0.27" and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml and import strum::Display.
Update get_files to return Vec<FileEntry> and loop with println!("{:?}", file) in main.
Pass &file.path() to fs::metadata so each entry gets its own size and directory flag.
common_mistakes: Calling fs::metadata(&path) instead of fs::metadata(&file.path()), which repeats the parent directory's size for every entry
Using {} instead of {:?} before implementing Display or Tabled on FileEntry
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String } fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) { if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&file.path()) { data.push(FileEntry { name: file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()), e_type: if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }, len_btyes: meta.len(), modified: "".to_string(), }); } }

steps.title: Format output in a styled table
steps.instructions: Add tabled = "0.20.0" to Cargo.toml and derive Tabled with #[tabled(rename = ...)] attributes on your file entry struct. Build a Table with Style::rounded(), apply column and row colors, and print it.

targets.caption: Create, style, and print the table

explanations.topic: Deriving Tabled to render structs as ASCII tables
Applying Style::rounded() and targeting Columns and Rows with Color

hints: Import Table, Tabled, and tabled::settings::{object::{Columns, Rows}, Color, Style}.
Make table mutable (let mut table = Table::new(...);) so you can call .with() and .modify().
Use #[tabled(rename = "Name")] above fields in FileEntry to override header names.
common_mistakes: Importing Color or Style from clap or owo_colors instead of tabled::settings
Forgetting to make table mutable before calling table.with(...) or table.modify(...)
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] struct FileEntry { #[tabled(rename = "Name")] name: String, #[tabled(rename = "Type")] e_type: EntryType, #[tabled(rename = "Size B")] len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } let get_files = get_files(&path); let mut table = Table::new(get_files); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(1), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modified timestamps using chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and convert meta.modified() into a DateTime<Utc> formatted with "%a %b %e %Y" when building each FileEntry. Run cargo run -- src to list the src directory with dates.

targets.caption: Convert SystemTime to formatted UTC date string
Set column 2 color to bright yellow

hints: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and import chrono::{DateTime, Utc}.
Use if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() to handle platforms where modification time is unavailable.
Call date.format("%a %b %e %Y") inside format!("{}", ...) to populate modified.
common_mistakes: Using mod as a variable name, which is a reserved Rust keyword (use modi instead)
Forgetting to annotate let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); so Rust knows the target type
steps.code: use chrono::{DateTime, Utc}; modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() }

steps.title: Add JSON output flag with serde
steps.instructions: Add serde (with derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, derive Serialize on your entry types, and add #[arg(short, long)] json: bool to the CLI struct. Print serde_json::to_string output when the json flag is set, otherwise print the table.

explanations.topic: Using #[arg(short, long)] on a bool field for CLI flags in clap
Deriving serde::Serialize on both FileEntry and nested EntryType

hints: Add serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } and serde_json = "1.0" to Cargo.toml.
Derive Serialize on both EntryType and FileEntry so serde_json::to_string can serialize them.
Add #[arg(short, long)] above json: bool in struct CLI so clap treats it as a flag instead of positional.
common_mistakes: Omitting #[arg(short, long)] on json: bool, which makes clap panic because bool cannot be a positional argument
Deriving Serialize on FileEntry without also deriving Serialize on EntryType
steps.code: #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, if cli.json { let get_files = get_files(&path); println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(path); }
